title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
slides: Lovable's $13.3B valuation—what does it actually mean?
The raise brings total funding to $400M fresh.
But its customer growth hides a critical churn risk.
You must now rethink your AI prototyping budget.
Audit your Lovable prototypes for hidden lock-in.
thread_text:
1. $13.3B, but churn lurks

Lovable's new valuation implies $13.3B, yet customer growth isn't the whole story—churn risk is rising.

2. Fresh $400M, same trap

The $400M raise fuels expansion, but lock-in tightens as users migrate prototypes, making exits costlier.

3. Your budget must shift

Prototyping with AI seems cheap, but hidden export limits and dependency costs inflate long-term expenses.

4. Audit before you build

Check if your Lovable prototypes have exportable code or rely on proprietary logic—lock-in starts silent.

5. Test your exit today

Try exporting one prototype now. If it fails, that's your answer on budget realignment.

A $13.3 billion valuation, but your prototypes might be the real cost. 🚨

Lovable just raised $400M at that new price tag, but the catch? Customer growth is hiding a rising churn risk. The tool gets you hooked fast, yet exiting gets pricier as your builds depend on its proprietary logic. 💸

For anyone prototyping with AI, your budget math just changed—cheap upfront can mean expensive lock-in later when export limits hit. ⚠️

Try exporting one of your existing Lovable prototypes right now. If it fails, that’s your answer on whether to keep building there. Have you tested your exit yet?
